name: Drift
description: A hardened, tapered steel punch. Driven through hot metal with a hammer, it opens and sizes a hole.
notes: A round bar 32 mm across and 235 mm long, tapering to a blunt point, with a heat-tinted mushroomed striking end. The quality name drifting is new: metalworking recipes call for a drift.

name: Electric forge
description: A benchtop electric furnace for heating metal to working heat. Plugged into the mains, it glows orange behind its door.
notes: A painted steel case 300 by 240 mm and 260 mm tall with a door over a glowing chamber, a control panel with display, dial and switch, and a mains cord. The box counts the cord and plug trailing behind; the case alone is about 19 l. It stands on a bench and runs off mains power, so it is a workstation; the size is a placeholder.

name: Gas forge
description: A propane forge: a lined steel drum on a stand with a burner in its top. It heats steel faster than coal and without the smoke.
notes: An insulated drum 280 mm across and 340 mm long on a welded stand, its mouth lined with fire brick and glowing, a burner tube with a brass air bell and a hose dropping to the floor. The box counts the stand, the burner and the hose. Forging 2 against the electric forge's 1 because it reaches welding heat. It needs a gas bottle, which has no fuel field here yet. The size is a placeholder.

name: Hot cut
description: A heavy chisel on a wooden handle. Set it on hot steel and strike it to cut the bar through.
notes: A 25 by 40 mm chisel head on a 300 mm handle, with a heat-tinted striking face and a bright edge. The box counts the air round the handle and head. The quality name hot_cutting is new: metalworking recipes call for a hot cut.

name: Bronze hot cut
description: A heavy bronze chisel on a wooden handle, for cutting through hot metal.
notes: Shares the steel hot cut's model with bronze on the head, face and edge. Made by a smith rather than found, so usage is empty.

name: Mild steel mail sheet
description: A sheet of riveted rings in mild steel. Joined with others and shaped, it becomes mail armour.
notes: A sheet 250 mm square laid flat with its rows of rings standing proud and one edge rolled. The steel grade variants and the platinum grille share this model, each with its own finishes.

name: Medium steel mail sheet
description: A sheet of riveted rings in medium steel. Joined with others and shaped, it becomes mail armour.
notes: Shares the mild steel sheet's model with steel-grey for the sheet. A smith's intermediate rather than a found item, so usage is empty.

name: High-carbon steel mail sheet
description: A sheet of riveted rings in high-carbon steel. Joined with others and shaped, it becomes mail armour.
notes: Shares the mild steel sheet's model with steel-blued for the sheet. A smith's intermediate rather than a found item, so usage is empty.

name: Hardened steel mail sheet
description: A sheet of riveted rings in hardened steel. Joined with others and shaped, it becomes mail armour.
notes: Shares the mild steel sheet's model with steel-hardened for the sheet. A smith's intermediate rather than a found item, so usage is empty.

name: Tempered steel mail sheet
description: A sheet of riveted rings in tempered steel. Joined with others and shaped, it becomes mail armour.
notes: Shares the mild steel sheet's model with steel-heat-tint for the sheet. A smith's intermediate rather than a found item, so usage is empty.

name: Platinum grille
description: A small sheet of woven platinum rings. Prized for electrodes and other delicate work.
notes: Shares the mail sheet's model in platinum. A real platinum grille is a fine mesh; at play distance the ring sheet stands in for it.

name: Sandleather
description: A patch of leather with sand worked into its rough side. Rubs a surface smooth when there is no sandpaper.
notes: A 90 by 60 mm leather patch with a sand layer and a small heap. Made by hand rather than found, so usage is empty. The quality name filing is new and shared with sandpaper. brick-buff stands in for sand; a sand finish would read better.

name: Iron mail sheet
description: A sheet of riveted rings in plain iron. Joined with others and shaped, it becomes mail armour.
notes: Otherwise the same as the mild steel sheet, so it rides on that model with iron-dull. Hand-made, so usage is empty.

name: Flat-jaw tongs
description: Long blacksmith's tongs with flat jaws. They hold hot metal on the anvil and in the fire.
notes: Tongs 440 mm long lying on their side: flat jaws, a riveted boss and round reins spreading at the ends. gripping 2, the tongs level, is for holding hot work in metalworking recipes.

name: Bronze flat-jaw tongs
description: Long bronze tongs with flat jaws, for holding hot metal.
notes: Shares the steel tongs' model in bronze. Made by a smith rather than found, so usage is empty.

name: Treadle grindstone
description: A sandstone wheel in a wooden frame, turned by a foot treadle. Grinds and sharpens steel without power.
notes: A 300 mm sandstone wheel on an iron axle between two posts of an oak frame 500 mm long, a crank and rod down to a treadle, and a water trough under the wheel. The frame is mostly air. It stands where it is put, so it is a workstation with grinding 2 and sharpening 1, as the powered grinding wheel has. brick-buff stands in for sandstone.

name: Sandpaper
description: A sheet of abrasive paper for smoothing wood and metal.
notes: A 230 by 280 mm sheet laid grit side up with one corner folded back to show the paper. The model draws the sheet at the 2 mm voxel floor, thicker than real paper, and the fold adds height.

name: Steel scraper
description: A hardened blade with a handle at each end, drawn towards you to shave metal flat.
notes: A 260 mm blade with a bright honed edge, cranked at each end into a turned walnut handle pointing back, like a small drawknife.

name: Polishing stone
description: A heavy slab of stone ground flat on top. Rub metal on it to smooth and polish it.
notes: A rough slab about 300 by 250 mm and 70 mm thick with lumpy sides and a smoother, paler ground top in stone-whet. A natural stone dressed by hand rather than a shop item, so usage is empty.

name: Swage and die set
description: A blacksmith's set of grooved blocks and dies, for rounding bars and forming heads on bolts and rivets.
notes: A bottom swage with a round groove and a square hardy shank, its top swage laid groove up on a steel rod handle with a ring end, and two round heading dies. The box counts the air round the long handle. The quality name swaging is new: metalworking recipes call for this set.

name: Kitchen tongs
description: Sprung steel tongs with scalloped ends, for turning food in the pan.
notes: Stainless tongs about 300 mm long lying open on their side, with a pull ring at the sprung end, rubber grips and toothed heads. Gripping 1, below the metalworking tongs' 2.
